title: Source Credibility Checker
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: AI-Native Schools
description: Rate eight fictional sources of evidence about an education product as Lead only, Use with caution, or Reasonable weight by applying a three-part rule.

learningObjectives: The learner will judge how much weight each of eight sources of evidence about an educational product deserves by applying the independence, review, and comparison-group rules, correctly rating at least seven of eight on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Independent evaluation, self-reported results, preprint, peer review, and comparison group, from Chapter 3.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Apply a rule, commit a rating, and read the reason
keyQuestions: Is there a comparison group studied at the same time?
Has the work been peer reviewed?
commonMisconceptions: A study paid for by a vendor can never be independent
A preprint is the same as a peer-reviewed paper
A comparison to national norms is a comparison group
assessmentOpportunities: Is a comparison with national norms a comparison group?
Can a vendor-paid study be independent?
What rating does an independent preprint of a randomized trial get?

controls.name: Three rating buttons
controls.description: Choose Lead only, Use with caution, or Reasonable weight for the current source.

controls.name: Show definitions
controls.description: Shows or hides the rule and the three ratings.

controls.name: Next
controls.description: Moves to the next source after feedback.

controls.name: Previous missed and Next missed
controls.description: On the results screen, step through the sources you missed.

controls.name: Play again
controls.description: Reshuffles the sources for a practice run.
